claims.says: A ledger can be checked by a verifier that imports no other Forge layer: it reimplements canonical JSON, SHA-256, did:key decoding and Ed25519 itself, so a bug in the layers that write a ledger cannot also hide in the one that checks it.
claims.source: canon-verify-layer/SPEC.md §1 (the zero-trust isolation rule) and its Function ("the zero-trust, standalone verifier"); SPEC_V2.md (agreement with ledger_v2, current 2.0.0).
claims.confirmed_how: "yes to all and commit" on claims/FIRST_CLAIMS_DRAFT.md
claims.expected_dry_run: unknown, not distrusted. It is rarely on a real path by design (it is the auditor), so it should be asked "why is this here?", and James's keep answer becomes its evidence.
